correctness.rationale: Take the longest Dyck suffix and split it at zero returns. Its core cannot itself have a Dyck suffix by concatenation. A legal cut cannot start strictly inside a primitive component because the remainder of that component then has strictly negative net balance, unchanged by later complete components. No cut can start before the maximal suffix. Earlier component counts after a legal deletion cannot acquire extra blocks since reattaching deleted blocks would contradict maximality. Hence the option values are exactly 0,…,k−1 by induction, including the empty word. The primitive series p(z) counts words aDb, and the unique core plus sequence factorization gives B=(1−p)/(1−2z) and F=B/(1−tp). A b-ending core must end at a strict new low: if its final height was visited before, the suffix from the last such visit is Dyck. Reverse these cores and remove their first downstep; the remaining walk is nonpositive, giving the claimed binomial by reflection. Words ending in a contribute 2^(n−1) separately. Minimum component length 2 forces the claimed extremizers and parity, with the empty case handled separately. Under the coupled reversed fair stream, an upstep at zero forbids any longer Dyck extension; each downstep at zero returns almost surely and renews the process. The finite component count stabilizes almost surely to the geometric law with mass 2^(−k−1). Independent bounded replay `python /workspace/review_replay.py 3` used bit-word option searches and mex on 8191 words through length 12, with the length-12 counts 2510,1024,386,130,37,8,1. Supplied checkers and recorded outputs were inspected, not executed; finite checks are not the general proof.
